mission: Regulate the expression of cellular defence genes in response to oxidative and electrophilic stress.

stage2a.operation: Cell mechanism and prepared-food exposure support bounded regulation; nasal targets are not direct brain efficacy. Mature-broccoli preparation join is held, while the specified disrupted-sprout source remains usable.

existing_findings.proposition: Keap1 represses Nrf2 until oxidative or electrophilic stress allows defence-gene transcription. Sulforaphane can slow Keap1-directed disposal of Nrf2 in cells. That is regulation, not a dietary requirement.

existing_source_assessments.label: Itoh et al. (1999)
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Keap1 binds the Neh2 domain of Nrf2 and represses antioxidant-response-element activity. Electrophiles oppose that repression.

assessment.study: Identification of Keap1 as the repressor of Nrf2, with tests of electrophilic agents in cells.
assessment.population: Transfected cell lines. No human cohort.
assessment.result: Keap1 holds Nrf2 back, and electrophiles release that hold so defence genes can be transcribed.
assessment.effect_magnitude: The paper reports repression and its release. It does not give a human fold change.
assessment.evidence_summary: Defence-gene transcription is a regulated response to oxidative and electrophilic stress.
assessment.limitations: Cell identification of the sensor is not a food result and not a brain measurement.

existing_source_assessments.label: Zhang et al. (2004)
existing_source_assessments.exposure_context: cells exposed to oxidative stress or sulforaphane
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Keap1 marks Nrf2 for disposal. Oxidative stress and sulforaphane inhibit that marking. A cysteine-151 mutant of Keap1 resists that inhibition.

assessment.study: Cell and biochemical tests of Keap1 as the adaptor that marks Nrf2 for disposal.
assessment.population: Cultured cells. No human dietary cohort.
assessment.result: Stress or sulforaphane slows disposal of Nrf2. Changing cysteine 151 of Keap1 blocks that effect.
assessment.effect_magnitude: The paper reports inhibition of ubiquitination, not a dietary dose.
assessment.evidence_summary: Sulforaphane acts on the Keap1 sensor in cells. It is not a nutrient the regulation requires.
assessment.limitations: Cell exposure to sulforaphane is not the sprout homogenate and not brain Nrf2.

existing_findings.disposition: Existing canonical assessment retained; enrichment is additive. No clinical or source-level negative inferred from bounded retrieval.

existing_findings.proposition: A myrosinase-completed broccoli sprout homogenate raised phase II enzyme RNA in nasal cells of healthy adults. Extracted sulforaphane capsules did not raise Nrf2 target-gene expression in COPD lung cells.

existing_source_assessments.label: Riedl, Saxon and Diaz-Sanchez (2009)
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Nasal phase II enzyme RNA rose with dose after three days of the homogenate. Alfalfa homogenate did not do this.

assessment.study: Placebo-style food comparison in healthy nonsmokers. Broccoli sprout homogenate versus alfalfa sprout homogenate, once daily for three days.
assessment.population: Healthy nonsmoking adults. Nasal cells sampled after the third dose.
assessment.result: Phase II enzyme RNA in nasal cells rose with the broccoli sprout dose and did not rise with alfalfa.
assessment.effect_magnitude: The rise was dose-related. Nrf2 protein was not measured, so no Nrf2 fold change is available.
assessment.evidence_summary: A defined sprout preparation can raise airway defence-gene RNA.
assessment.limitations: Airway RNA is not brain Nrf2, not an ordinary broccoli serving, and not a clinical outcome.

existing_source_assessments.label: Wise et al. (2016)
existing_source_assessments.exposure_context: capsules of sulforaphane extracted from broccoli sprouts
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Four weeks of 25 or 150 micromoles of extracted sulforaphane did not raise Nrf2 target genes in COPD lung cells.

assessment.study: Randomised comparison of two sulforaphane capsule doses with placebo for four weeks.
assessment.result: Nrf2 target-gene expression in alveolar macrophages and bronchial epithelium did not rise. Inflammation markers and lung function did not differ.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No rise in the measured target genes at either 25 or 150 micromoles a day.
assessment.evidence_summary: Extracted sulforaphane capsules did not reproduce the homogenate gene result.
assessment.limitations: COPD lung cells are not healthy nasal cells, and capsules are not the myrosinase-completed homogenate.

existing_findings.disposition: Existing canonical assessment retained; enrichment is additive. No clinical or source-level negative inferred from bounded retrieval.

preserved_phenome_source_records.rationale: Verlaet reviews a rationale for dietary antioxidant treatment in ADHD. The human measurement is nasal defence-gene expression after a prepared sprout homogenate, not a cognitive result.
The human exposure changed phase II enzyme RNA in nasal cells. It does not show that ordinary repeated eating changes attention, and the sources do not compare repeated exposure with a single dose.
Nrf2-dependent detoxification and antioxidant gene programmes may intersect stress-buffering redox context; direct ADHD stress-outcome evidence remains limited.

type_delivery_metadata.permitted_wording: Sulforaphane is a Direct Regulatory Modulator of KEAP1–Nrf2. Food-derived exposure increased Nrf2-associated gene expression in human nasal cells under the tested preparation; brain engagement and ADHD benefit are not established.
type_delivery_metadata.evidence_limitation: Preparation-, tissue- and population-specific target engagement; no ordinary-serving efficacy, essentiality or brain/ADHD benefit claim.

all_existing_inputs.preservation_note: The rapid manuscript selection is not the canonical inventory. Absence from that selection changes no accepted status or source record.

existing_practices.biological_role: Three daily doses of broccoli sprouts, blended with water and daikon sprouts and held at 37°C so myrosinase could finish forming sulforaphane, increased phase II enzyme RNA in nasal cells of healthy adults. The authors read that shared pattern as Nrf2-linked induction. They did not measure Nrf2 protein or its movement into the nucleus.
existing_practices.evidence_limitation: This is three days of that homogenate in healthy adults and nasal enzyme RNA, not brain Nrf2, an ordinary broccoli serving, or the four-week sprout-extract capsules that did not raise lung target-gene expression in COPD.
